name: Salon Booking Bot — Drill State Read

nodes.name: Sticky — what this is and is not

parameters.content:
## Drill state read — TEST SUPPORT, read-only
`tests/run-d11.sh` must assert on the DATA, not on status codes. This returns `stage|last_intent|markerCount`
for one record and nothing else: no name, no phone, no message, no sender_key.

**Why an endpoint and not a read-only Airtable PAT** (the alternative, weighed): a PAT is a long-lived
credential that can read the WHOLE base — every table, all the PII — and it would have to live in a file on
the build host. This reaches exactly three fields, requires the Cloudflare Access service token AND a valid
HMAC over the body, and writes nothing. The smaller surface won.

⚠ **The `owner-` prefix is there for a MEASURED reason, not for tidiness.** Published first as
`/webhook/drill-state`, all three probes — owner token, api token, and NO token at all — reached this
workflow and were stopped only by the signature gate: `/webhook/*` is Access-EXEMPT by design, so that
path had ONE layer while the note beside it claimed two. Moved under `/webhook/owner-*`, which the
CP 6d-0 Access application covers, and re-measured: no token now gets Cloudflare's own 403.

⚠ `read_drill_state` is deliberately NOT in `OWNER_ACTIONS`. That list holding exactly ONE verb is what makes
the write path auditable; widening it so a test could read would have traded the security model for convenience.
